holidays.name: National Taco Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble taco in all its folded glory. Crunchy, soft, breakfast, fish, or street-style: every taco is welcome, and many restaurants run deals to mark the occasion.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance in the United States. Its exact origin is unclear, but it has become a firm fixture on the American food calendar.
holidays.funFact: Tacos are widely thought to predate the arrival of Europeans in Mexico. Some food historians say the word comes from the silver miners' term for the paper-wrapped gunpowder charges they used.

holidays.name: Kanelbullens dag (Cinnamon Bun Day)
holidays.description: Sweden's yearly salute to the cinnamon bun, or kanelbulle. Bakeries and home kitchens fill with the smell of cardamom, cinnamon and sugar, and it's a good excuse for a fika coffee break.
holidays.origin: The day was created in 1999 by the Swedish Home Baking Council to mark its 40th anniversary. It quickly became a beloved national tradition.
holidays.funFact: Swedes are some of the world's biggest cinnamon bun fans. Many Swedish kanelbullar are flavored with cardamom as well as cinnamon, and they're often shaped into a knot rather than a spiral.

holidays.name: World Animal Day
holidays.description: A global day for animal welfare, when people support shelters, wildlife groups and pet adoption. Many also take it as a chance to give their furry roommates extra treats.
holidays.origin: It began in 1925 at a conference in Berlin. The date was chosen to coincide with the feast day of Saint Francis of Assisi, the patron saint of animals.
holidays.funFact: The day also opens World Space Week, so it's a rare date that honors both critters and cosmonauts.
